analyst_view.overall: Early view: a Breton derby between sides with opposite styles: Lorient (10th) have the second-best defence (8 conceded) and the weakest shooting in the league, while Rennes' games have produced 42 goals in 10. Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice and 2-1 at home to Lille, play at NEC in the Europa League four days later, and were hoping to have top scorer Esteban Lepaul back from an ankle problem.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: Lorient's games have averaged under two goals (9 scored, 8 conceded) and Alexandre Dujeux's side has kept clean sheets in most of its away games, so they will try to make this tight at home too. Rennes concede plenty (21), which is the risk to this view, but Lorient create the fewest big chances in the league.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Season averages fit: Rennes win 5.7 a game (3rd) and Lorient 3.7. Rennes will probably have more of the ball, so most corners should come from them.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean slightly higher because it is a derby, even though Lorient are among the cleanest sides (9.3 fouls a game). Derby edge plus Rennes' frustration if they cannot break Lorient down usually brings bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. I stay close to it: Rennes take 16.2 shots a game (3rd) and Lorient 10.3 (17th), which sums to roughly the site's figure. Lorient failed to register a shot on target in two straight league games before winning at Le Havre.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Lorient are last in the league for shots on target (2.8 a game), and Rennes managed only two on target from 15 shots against Lille. If Lepaul is back that improves Rennes' finishing, so this is worth rechecking with team news.
